turns.input: What temperature condition triggers an alert in chilled storage?
turns.expected_output: An alert is triggered when temperature stays above 6°C for more than 10 consecutive minutes.
context: The chilled-grocery storage target is 2-6 degrees Celsius. A temperature alert is raised when a monitored location is above 6 degrees Celsius for more than 10 consecutive minutes. A quality hold is mandatory when the measured temperature is above 8 degrees Celsius for more than 5 consecutive minutes. The quality hold remains active until a documented release decision is recorded by the Quality Lead.
“More than” is strict. Exactly 10 minutes above 6 C is not sufficient for an alert; exactly 5 minutes above 8 C is not sufficient for the mandatory hold.

turns.input: We received 197 units of an SKU instead of the expected 200. Must we escalate it?
turns.expected_output: No. The shortage is three units, or 1.5%, so it exceeds neither the more-than-three-unit threshold nor the more-than-2% threshold.
context: Escalate a variance to Inventory Control when the absolute difference is greater than three units OR greater than 2% of expected quantity. Exactly three missing units do not trigger the unit threshold, but can still trigger the percentage threshold.

For example, receiving 97 units against 100 expected creates a three-unit, 3% shortage and therefore requires escalation. Receiving 197 against 200 expected creates a three-unit, 1.5% shortage and does not cross either escalation threshold. Negative and positive variances follow the same rule.
